newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Escotel Mobile achieves financial closure.
newsitem.headline: India's Escotel Mobile achieves financial closure.

text.p: India's Escotel Mobile Communications Ltd has become the first zonal cellular telephone services operator to achieve financial closure, a company official said on Monday.
"We have achieved financial closure. Both domestic and foreign debt has been tied up," Escotel's chief operating officer, Chris Edwards, told Reuters.
Escotel is a 51:49 joint venture between India's Escorts Ltd and Hong Kong's First Pacific Company Ltd.

"The total project cost for the first four years of operation is $253 million. Domestic debt is 1.25 billion rupees ($34.9 million), foreign debt is $128 million, and the equity capital is $90 million," said Edwards.
The domestic debt is being placed by Infrastructure Leasing and Financial Services Ltd (ILFS). The foreign debt, needed to finance equipment cost, is being placed by Chase Manhattan, he added.

Cellular companies face resistance from domestic lenders unconvinced about the viability of zonal licences because of the high fees licensees must pay to the government and promoters' unwillingness to stand guarantor.

"We've stayed away from Indian financial institutions as we wanted a quick financial closure, but have got guarantees from both promoters. ILFS will provide 400 million rupees of the debt, and place the rest," said Sanjay Sethi, ILFS senior manager.

HDFC Bank and General Electric arm GE Capital are expected to be part of the lending consortium. Escotel will start repayment from 2000/2001, and will pay about 18 percent interest per annum from the first year, he added.

Escotel has the licences for the zones of Haryana, Kerala, and Uttar Pradesh West. The Indian government auctioned licences for telecommunications services as part of an economic liberalisation programme launched in 1991.

The company was one of the first zonal cellular operators to launch services, after deciding in February 1996 on Lucent Technologies as its network supplier. Escotel provides services in 23 cities and is in the process of adding another 10 cities to its network.
"We have 18,000 subscribers in all three zones, and expect to increase this number to 200,000 subscribers by the end of year four," said Edwards.
"Based on our projections, Escotel should achieve cash break-even after three years of operation, and be in the black in four years," Sethi said.
